judge_assessment.explanation: Every value the judge lists is correct: A'' = (5, 1); P''Q'' = 5 from (-4,-1) to (-7,3); A''B'' = 3 and the midpoint of A''C'' is (2.5, -2); the parallel mirrors x = 1 and x = 4 give a 6-unit translation; the midpoint of P and P'' is the origin; both triangle areas are 6; the hexagon has 6 lines and a 60 deg smallest rotation; and both diagonals of EFGH share the midpoint (3, 1.5). The judge's five manual items are also genuinely present and well specified. What the judge did not check is the INTERMEDIATE image in each composition, and that is where the packet leaks. Problem 1 prints "After the reflection, A' = (__,__)" for A(3,4) - A' = (3,-4) - and verify.json id 1 contains only the two entries that produce A''(5,1). Problem 4 prints P' = (__,__): P' = (2,2) appears nowhere in verify.json, not even as a distance datum. Problem 7 prints M' = (__,__) (M' = (7,2), unverified) and then a bare \underline writing rule for "Would you get the same final point doing the two steps the other way round?", which is an open response with no entry of any kind. Separately, problems 1, 2, 3 and 7 end with an extra unlabelled "Answer: ____" (an explicit \par\vspace*{1.2cm}\ansline after the per-part blanks), which on problems 1 and 7 has no owner at all.

strengths_to_preserve: The sheet's instructional spine is deliberate and it works: problems 1-3 do a composition, 4-6 name the single transformation it amounts to, and 8-10 turn that machinery on a figure's own symmetries - and the key's opening paragraph tells the grader exactly that, plus the fact that a rotation named without a centre is not an answer.

The manual descriptors are the best in this batch: problem 6's entry pre-accepts "rotation 90 deg clockwise" and "rotation 270 deg counterclockwise", and explicitly refuses 90 deg counterclockwise as the other order of the composition - a distinction a hurried grader would miss.
Problem 10's manual entry demands a GENERAL argument and states that re-checking the single point K from part (a) is not sufficient, which is the difference between a justification and an example.

Problem 4's declared trap (3, the gap between the mirrors) sits next to the verified answer 6, so the key's Common wrong answers block names the twice-the-gap theorem instead of marking the answer wrong.

root_causes.description: Only the terminal image of each composition was declared. The intermediate images carry their own printed blanks and are the whole point of "do the two steps in the order given", yet they were treated as scratch work.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 1 prints "After the reflection, A' = ($~\ansblank$,$~\ansblank$)"; verify.json id 1 has two entries, a+b at a=3,b=2 -> 5 and -c+d at c=4,d=5 -> 1, both parts of A''.
verify.json id 4 holds a distance on [[0,2],[6,2]] and a manual entry; the printed P' = (2, 2) appears in no entry.
verify.json id 7 holds -(a+b) -> -7 and -(c+d) -> -2 (that is M''); the printed M' = (7, 2) is unverified.
answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row 1 is "5, 1" - the key's prose gives A' = (3, -4) but the grading column cannot show it.

root_causes.description: A yes/no-plus-reason question printed with its own writing rule was not routed to manual review because the problem already carried machine-checked coordinates.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7 ends with "Would you get the same final point doing the two steps the other way round?" followed by \underline{\hspace{1.6cm}}; verify.json id 7 has no `manual` entry. (The answer is no: translate-then-half-turn gives (-7,-2) while half-turn-then-translate gives (3,-4).)

root_causes.description: The document adds a trailing \ansline by hand after per-part blanks, defeating the preamble's self-clearing flag whose whole purpose is to suppress exactly that orphan blank.
evidence: worksheet.tex problems 1, 2, 3 and 7 all end with "\par\vspace*{1.2cm}\ansline" although their stems already contain \ansblank for every requested value.
worksheet.pdf shows the resulting unlabelled "Answer: ____" under problems 1, 2, 3 and 7.
templates/worksheet-preamble.tex documents the intent: \ansblank clears the flag so "the parent's single trailing line is suppressed".

improvements.title: Verify (or flag manual for) every response slot the worksheet prints
improvements.proposed_change: Make the verify JSON an inventory of PRINTED RESPONSES, not of terminal answers. SKILL.md should require one verify entry per answer location a problem prints (\ansblank, \ansline, \answerline, an \underline writing rule, or a table cell the student fills), with `manual` used where the response is not a value. Enforce it with a new gate wired into scripts/build.sh that segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.segment_spans, counts the answer-location macros and fill-in rules per problem, and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries for the same problem id. Here the gate must fail problems 1, 4 and 7, whose printed intermediate-image blanks (A', P', M') have no verify entry.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem prints five \ansblank slots against a verify id carrying four entries must make the new gate exit non-zero; adding the missing entry (or a `manual` entry) must make it exit 0. Today no gate compares slot count with entry count, so the fixture passes the whole chain - the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic gap in this run: a sheet can no longer claim complete verification while printing blanks nothing checked, and the answer key's Quick Answers bank stops shipping short rows.
improvements.risk: Sheets that use several blanks to scaffold ONE value ("x-coordinate: __ y-coordinate: __ so P' = (__, __)") will need either a coarser blank layout or a documented per-value grouping, so the gate needs a same-value exemption to avoid false failures.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problem 7's "other way round?" rule must force a `manual` entry; the five existing manual descriptors show the author already writes them well when the item is recognised.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

improvements.title: One answer blank per requested value - no lumped blank, no orphan blank
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md's "Answer location (every problem gets one)" should read "every REQUESTED VALUE gets one": a multi-part problem ends each part with its own \ansline/\answerline inside the stem (which already suppresses \problem's automatic blank, as the preamble documents), and no problem emits a trailing unlabelled blank once every part already has one. Extend tests/check_answer_line.py, which today only binds units, to compare answer-location macros against the distinct non-manual verify entries for the problem id and fail in both directions. Here the fix is the other direction: drop the hand-written trailing \ansline on problems 1, 2, 3 and 7 and let the preamble's suppression do its job.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair for tests/check_answer_line.py: (a) a problem printing one \ansline against four verify entries must exit non-zero, and (b) the same problem with one \ansline per part must exit 0; plus (c) a problem whose parts all carry blanks and which then emits a trailing \ansline must exit non-zero. All three pass today because the checker never counts blanks.
improvements.expected_impact: The student knows where each requested value goes and the grader can map a Quick Answers row onto the sheet position by position.
improvements.risk: Per-part blanks consume vertical space, so a few dense sheets will gain a page; the gate must also allow a deliberate \noansline on sketch/proof items.

case_summary: The most thorough sheet in the batch - ten problems that move coherently from compositions to one-step names to figure symmetry, with five carefully written manual descriptors and a key that tells the grader what a complete description must contain. All twelve machine values recompute correctly. The gap is that only the FINAL image of each composition is verified: the printed intermediate blanks for A', P' and M' are unchecked, problem 7's order-matters question is an unflagged open response, and four problems ship an orphan trailing answer blank.
